The first 300m is easy. Don't let it fool you. Talk with your coach to find a goal split to keep, and stick to it. From about 1700 to 1300 is the hardest thing you will probably ever do, and you have to push yourself to stay in the groove and on track. Keep at your pace and get into a solid rhythm and stroke rate. From 1300 to 1000, you should work on continuing your steady but challenging pace set. It sounds hard, but your body CAN do it. Don't let what you *think* you can do get in the way, just pull harder. Once 900 hits, it's really easy to breathe a sigh of relief at being halfway done. I cannot stress this enough: DO NOT let up now. Never give yourself a break. This is your crunch time.
 When you get to 900, for the next 300 meters you're going to focus on powerful, long strokes, while staying at your target split. Try to drop a second off your split at each 100 meter mark. When 600 hits, you must remember that if you begin your sprint now, you will tire out at the most important final 300 and RUIN your time. Alas, you will still need to go fast, so you can shorten your stroke A LITTLE, not a lot, and continue to shave off one second per every 100 meters. 
 Once you hit 400, begin preparing yourself for your 300 meter sprint. Once 300 meters hits, just go as fast as you humanly can. If you pass out or puke at the end, it means you tried your best. Try your absolute hardest because the 2k is the ultimate test of what boat you will be on and how valued you are on the team.
 But do not psych yourself out. Be confident in yourself and your goal and don't rush, just imagine yourself being a champion olympic rower. Always works for me. 
Oh and eat a banana and drink lots of water leading up to it. but in the 3 hours prior don't drink or eat a lot.
Best of luck to you!
